headline: Law extends a National Institutes of Health program that funds research on childhood diseases through 2028.
what_it_does: This law renews a children's disease research program at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) through fiscal year 2028. It requires the NIH to coordinate its research on children's health so different efforts do not repeat each other. The Department of Health and Human Services must also report to Congress on the research paid for by the program.

who_it_affects.group: Children with serious diseases and their families
who_it_affects.how: Research into childhood diseases funded by this NIH program continues through 2028.

who_it_affects.group: Medical researchers who study children's diseases
who_it_affects.how: They can keep seeking funding from this NIH program, which must now coordinate its work to avoid overlap.

who_it_affects.group: National Institutes of Health and Department of Health and Human Services
who_it_affects.how: NIH must coordinate its pediatric research, and HHS must report to Congress on research funded through the program.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 4, 2025; the program is reauthorized through fiscal year 2028.
